title: How a catalog entry becomes reusable
html:
How a catalog entry becomes reusable

Each entry keeps its contract in the main file’s header: its ID, summary, files and dependencies. adp_catalog.py build turns those headers into catalog.json; drift checks header/index agreement. publish_catalog.py stages publication plans and an About page through welcome.html; it does not publish by itself. Read the entry’s API before taking it, then verify its files actually load in the destination.

title: Templates are recipes, not deployed pages
html:
Templates are recipes, not deployed pages

template.json declares inheritance and the starting files. Starter supplies a shell, content, a part script and page styles. Assistant builds on it with an agent pane and canvas styles; Default inherits Assistant and adds its own entrypoint and kit selection. The HTML, CSS and JavaScript recipes ship with a .txt suffix, removed by adp.py new. The generated page still needs its host’s publication and record workflow.

title: What the local emulators stand in for
html:
What the local emulators stand in for

adp_dev.py serves a local Claude-like viewer; adp_dev.js supplies its browser shim. Records, queued messages and heartbeat files live under .adp-dev/. An agent uses dev watch and dev send to exercise the loop. The Sites localhost server is separate and exercises its Worker with local SQLite. A passing harness does not establish hosted access, durability or an unattended CLI connection.

title: Moving records does not move source
html:
Moving records does not move source

An export bundle contains seed packs, source metadata and native revisions. import-plan compares those records with fresh destination reads and classifies create, replace, skip or hold. Source revisions remain evidence; destination revisions guard writes. import-ack records confirmed outcomes. These commands do not automatically synchronize hosts or deploy a Site’s source.

title: Two adapter layers, one native authority
html:
Two adapter layers, one native authority

Browser adapters such as adapters/claude.js and openai-sites.js connect page code to a host. Offline adapters such as adp_claude_adapter.py translate the planner’s read/write plans and receipts. The Sites Worker stores records in D1 using the shipped SQL schema. Its fixture is a test page, not production membership setup. Access and revision checks stay on the server.

title: Root files: purpose, policy and provenance
html:
Root files: purpose, policy and provenance

README.md is the entrypoint; CONTRIBUTING.md explains setup and checks. SECURITY.md routes vulnerability reports privately, while CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md sets participation standards. LICENSE, NOTICE and CITATION.cff retain licensing and attribution. .gitignore keeps generated/local state out; ruff.toml, .gitleaks.toml and .pre-commit-config.yaml configure lint, secret scanning and local hooks.

title: Plugin updates and bundle releases are different
html:
Plugin updates and bundle releases are different

.claude-plugin/plugin.json names the plugin and points discovery at the base skill and road skills. It deliberately has no version: plugin installs follow the repository commit. The separately packaged adp.skill release uses the base skill’s metadata.version. A plugin manifest change and a tagged bundle release are separate operations.

title: What GitHub and local hooks actually run
html:
What GitHub and local hooks actually run

On pushes and pull requests, ci.yml checks secrets, Ruff, the unittest suite, skill packaging, catalog consistency and the catalog roundtrip. Local pre-commit/pre-push hooks configure related checks; their presence does not prove installation or execution. Issue/PR templates collect change and check details. Dependabot proposes GitHub Actions dependency updates weekly. The tag-triggered release workflow has its own checks and publishing permission.

title: Tests describe verification boundaries
html:
Tests describe verification boundaries

tests/ covers command plans, setup and packaging, templates, catalog/hash parity, record transfer, host adapters and local Worker/bridge fixtures. tools/roundtrip.py checks the catalog’s build/take/seed/preview path; CI runs it separately. Passing a fixture is evidence for that fixture, not every production host, browser or authenticated agent. Record the actual run and keep unobserved behavior explicit.

title: Release procedure versus historical release notes
html:
Release procedure versus historical release notes

RELEASING.md describes the bundle build, tag/version match and checksum verification. A v* tag triggers release.yml, which checks, builds and creates a release with adp.skill and its checksum. The checklist and v2.0.0 draft notes are historical working documents: they still contain old file counts and claims such as a missing license. Compare those claims with the current tree and CI; do not copy them into a current release receipt.
